Subject: Marketplace listing questions for Nimbus POC

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Nimbus is excited about Redwood's latency profile. Procurement and engineering asked for a concise plan for marketplace entry so they can budget runway and confirm co-sell eligibility. Specifically:

- Which SKU variants do you recommend we list for an initial pilot on AWS, Azure, and GCP?
- Which regions should be gating for the pilot vs GA?
- If we need to fall back from a premium SKU (quantized, multi-GPU) to a compatible variant, what's the customer impact and how is it surfaced in the marketplace listing?

Procurement also asked whether listing in AWS Marketplace triggers any additional onboarding with AWS GTM — Tom I cc'd you for visibility.

Would you be able to send a one-page eligibility matrix and a short execution plan by early next week?

Thanks,
Ana Torres
Head of Integrations, Nimbus Analytics

Subject: Re: Marketplace listing questions for Nimbus POC

Hi Ana — thanks for the clear list. I sketched an initial approach below and attached a draft SKU eligibility matrix. High level: prioritize a single, conservative pilot SKU per cloud that maps to Redwood's "Standard" offering (8-vCPU equivalent, single-GPU, int8 quantization option). That minimizes procurement friction and keeps co-sell alignment simple.

Quick answers: 
- Pilot SKUs (recommended):
  - AWS: redwood-standard-us-east-1 (single-GPU, int8 opt)
  - Azure: redwood-standard-eastus (single-GPU)
  - GCP: redwood-standard-us-central1 (single-GPU)

- Regions for pilot: us-east-1 (AWS), eastus (Azure), us-central1 (GCP) — pick one primary region per cloud where we already have capacity and established latency SLAs.

- Fallback behavior and customer impact:
  - Automatic fallback to a compatible "compat" SKU (e.g., redwood-compat-1) occurs when requested premium capacity is unavailable. The marketplace listing should clearly state the fallback policy and estimated delta (latency + per-token cost). For Nimbus' use case, delta is typically +20–60ms tail latency and ~5–10% higher cost on token-heavy workloads.

Next steps (proposed):
1) We finalize SKU names and attach a clean SKU_eligibility_matrix_Q2_2027.xlsx for your procurement.
2) Marissa will formalize listing packaging + a short blurb for each marketplace listing (1–2 sentences).
3) Rafael will coordinate the AWS co-sell intake so Tom can route to the right GTM contacts.

Marissa/ Rafael / Karthik — can you confirm capacity & any regional constraints? Ana — I attached the draft matrix. If that looks right, we'll convert it to the formal listing assets and a DocuSign purchase blueprint.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Marketplace listing questions for Nimbus POC

Thanks Grace — added a few concrete packaging suggestions and a fallback messaging draft. Full notes below. I'm attaching a short proposal PDF that you can share with procurement.

Marissa's packaging recommendations (concise):
- Offer tiers across clouds but keep pilot simple: "Standard" pilot SKU (listed above) + optional "Burst" SKU for Dedicated customers.
- Marketplace listing copy should include a single-line fallback statement under "Additional details":
  "If the requested capacity is temporarily unavailable, requests will be routed to a compatible variant with no data transfer — expect minor latency differences and a temporary change in unit pricing; contact support for guaranteed reserved throughput."

Cloud-specific considerations:
- AWS: Allow listing to reference an AWS co-sell-approved case study (once signed) — this accelerates GTM. Rafael, once you confirm intake, we should submit the co-sell package in parallel to listing prep.
- Azure: Need an explicit managed-identity example in the listing's docs for gov/commercial customers — call out in the listing's "How it works" section.
- GCP: Recommend a short note that customers can choose region at purchase time; default region will be us-central1.

Procurement & billing notes for Nimbus:
- We will publish SKU pricing bands (monthly metered + per-token). Procurement can select committed capacity via Redwood Dedicated if they want a flat invoice and reserved SLA.

Attached: proposal_nimbus_entry_plan_v1.pdf (one-page plan) and a cleaned SKU_eligibility_matrix.

On quoting and next steps: Grace — if Ana gives a quick greenlight on the matrix, Rafael and I will start the marketplace intake forms this week.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Director, Marketplace Programs, Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposal_nimbus_entry_plan_v1.pdf, SKU_eligibility_matrix_Q2_2027.xlsx
